title: mysql-ops-mcp: a read-only-first MCP server for agent access to SSH-only MySQL databases
description:
A Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that lets an AI agent query a private MySQL database — and, only if explicitly enabled, operate the server it lives on.

Built for the common real-world case where the database has no public port and no VPN, only SSH: the server opens and maintains its own SSH tunnel (pure paramiko), exposes the data as MCP tools, and refuses any statement that is not a single read statement. 17 tools are registered by default and all are read-only; state-changing tools (restart, deploy backend, deploy frontend) are not registered at all unless an opt-in flag is set, and are additionally gated by a container allowlist.

Statement validation runs before execution: single-statement only, comments stripped, rows capped. 24 unit tests cover the SQL guard, including comment-smuggling and stacked-statement attempts, and need no database.

The SQL guard is a backstop, not the primary control: the documented deployment is a read-only database account.
